explain.say: Ever tried to undo a tight wheel nut? You grab the far end of the spanner, not the middle. That is because turning depends on two things: how hard you push and how far from the pivot you push. That turning effect is called a moment. Let us see it on a seesaw.

explain.say: On the left, 300 newtons sits 2 metres from the pivot: a moment of 600 newton metres, turning anticlockwise. Look at the left side of the balance. How much moment does the right side need to stop the turning?

explain.say: Exactly 600 newton metres! The right side has 200 newtons at 3 metres, which is also 600, clockwise. Clockwise equals anticlockwise, so it balances. That is the principle of moments. Could a smaller force balance it from further out?

draw.text: 200 N × 3 m = 600 N·m, so it balances

explain.say: Yes, that is why long spanners help! Now a special case: a couple, two equal forces in opposite directions that do not line up. Your hands on a steering wheel push up on one side and down on the other. Look: the arrows cancel, so the wheel does not move sideways. But does it turn?

draw.text: Couple C = F × d = 40 N × 0.4 m = 16 N·m
The two forces cancel, but the turning does not

explain.say: It does! A couple gives pure turning and no push. With 40 newtons per hand on a 0.4 metre wheel, that is 16 newton metres. A couple has the same moment about every point, which makes it handy in exams. Challenge: what couple do you make turning a tap with 5 newtons per finger, 4 centimetres apart?

faq.q: What is the moment of a force?
faq.a: It is the turning effect of a force about a point: the force times the perpendicular distance from the point to the force's line of action. Its unit is the newton metre.

faq.q: What is the principle of moments?
faq.a: For a body in balance, the total clockwise moment about any point equals the total anticlockwise moment about that point.
Two forces of equal size, opposite direction and different lines of action. Together they produce turning but no overall push, and their moment is one force times the distance between them.

faq.q: Why is a long spanner easier to use?
faq.a: A longer handle gives a bigger perpendicular distance, so the same moment needs a smaller force from your hand.
asks: why do longer levers need less force

faq.q: Does the moment of a couple depend on the point I choose?
faq.a: No. A couple has the same moment about every point in the plane, which is why it is called a free vector.
asks: is a couple a free vector

facts: A couple produces rotation with zero resultant force.
The SI unit of moment and of torque is the newton metre.

quiz.say: You push with 150 newtons at right angles to a spanner, 0.3 metres from the nut. What moment do you apply?
quiz.show: 150 N applied at 90° to a spanner, 0.3 m from the nut. Moment?

wrong.1: That divides the force by the distance instead of multiplying.
wrong.2: Force and distance are multiplied, not added.

quiz.say: What does a couple do to a body that is free to move?
quiz.show: A couple acting on a free body causes…

options.show: Only sliding in a straight line
options.say: Only sliding in a straight line

quiz.why: The two forces cancel, so there is no overall push, only turning.

wrong.1: Sliding needs an unbalanced force, and a couple's forces cancel.
wrong.2: There is no net force, so the centre of mass does not accelerate.
